title: Harbour project memory demonstration
authorization_basis: The user requested this newly authored synthetic engineering demonstration through the project owner on 23 October 2026. This authorizes creating the demo; it is not independent human verification of its reference inventory.
data_origin: AI-assisted fictional dialogue authored for a product presentation and reproducible engineering example; not participant data, LongMemEval or a benchmark.

messages.content: I live in Adelaide. I generally prefer Python for backend projects. This semester I am keeping notes on two separate software projects, Harbour and Orchard, alongside ordinary personal plans. Please keep the project names attached to technical details because their requirements are not interchangeable.
Thanks. What is Harbour starting from, and which delivery dates or interface choices are already known?

The Harbour capstone backend currently uses MySQL. The original deadline for the Harbour capstone is 14 March 2026. Those are the arrangements at the start of this week; I expect to hear from the course coordinator before the next planning meeting.
That gives us a starting point. If a requirement changes, please name the project and describe what changed.

The Harbour web frontend uses TypeScript. Harbour's public forms must support keyboard-only navigation. We have a small review session planned for the interface, but nobody has completed that session yet. I am arranging the sample screens rather than claiming the accessibility review is finished.
You could consider Go for Harbour if the course permits it. This is only a suggestion, not an adopted decision or a change I have made.

I have not adopted your suggestion to move Harbour to Go. For the Harbour capstone backend, the course requires Java only. That is a project-specific course constraint, even though my usual backend preference is different. Please do not treat the earlier suggestion as our implementation plan.
Understood. Is Orchard part of that course deliverable, or does it have a different team and separate requirements?

For the unrelated Orchard inventory service, the team requires Rust. Orchard is a separate volunteer project, not another name for the Harbour capstone. Its team-specific requirement takes precedence over my general language preference when I work on Orchard, without changing the Harbour course requirement.
Would you like a break from the project discussion? I can suggest lunch ideas or help make a meeting list.

I follow a vegetarian diet. For lunch I am just considering places near the library; I have not booked anything. Food suggestions are separate from our technical work, and there is no need to bring my diet into decisions about programming languages, databases or deployment.
You might consider lentil soup or a vegetable wrap. Those are suggestions, not meals you have ordered.

We have migrated the Harbour capstone backend to PostgreSQL, and MySQL is no longer used for that backend. The migration is complete. This replaces the earlier database arrangement for Harbour; it does not describe Orchard or a temporary example on somebody else's laptop.
Thanks for the update. Has the coordinator said anything new about timing for the remaining capstone work?

The coordinator has moved the Harbour capstone deadline to 21 March 2026, replacing the original 14 March 2026 deadline. This is a confirmed course change, not my preferred extension or a tentative request. Other project dates were not part of the announcement.
Which deployment documents is the team using? You could bring their exact requirements to the next meeting.

The current Harbour deployment plan says its production region is North, and that plan is still active. This note concerns the production deployment, not a local development machine or an illustration in a tutorial. I am checking it against the client paperwork.
You could compare it with the signed client brief. I cannot obtain a revised approval or change the deployment for you.

The signed client brief, which is also still active, specifies the South region for that same Harbour production deployment. Both region documents are still active, and I have not established which one controls Harbour's production deployment. Neither has been withdrawn or declared to supersede the other.
You could ask the project owner to reconcile the documents in writing. Has any other document difference come up?

The active Harbour security brief requires OAuth for client authentication. It concerns the client-facing integration rather than administrator sign-in. I copied this requirement from the brief while preparing the meeting notes, and I am still comparing the separate integration handoff.
Does the handoff address that same client-facing integration? A difference in scope might matter to the discussion.

The active Harbour integration handoff requires API keys for client authentication. It addresses the same client-facing integration as the security brief. Both authentication documents remain active; I have not established whether OAuth or API keys controls the Harbour client integration. There is no agreed priority or replacement decision yet.
You could add that difference to the agenda. I have not changed a document, chosen a method or contacted the owner.

For an unrelated weekend exercise I sketched a tiny library catalogue on paper. A friend mentioned SQLite in a tutorial, and I borrowed a blue umbrella on the way home. None of that was a database change to either project. I may try the exercise later, but I have not started building it.
You might keep those tutorial notes in a separate notebook, away from the capstone meeting papers.

I am preparing a short Harbour team meeting agenda and checking the original documents again. I might take a coastal walk afterwards if the weather is dry, but that outing is only a possibility. For now I want the technical notes kept distinct from lunch ideas, travel possibilities and casual examples.
I can help format the agenda with open questions and follow-up owners. Personal plans can stay in separate notes.
